items.statement: Digital Citizenship
Students harness the possibilities afforded by technology to gain and share the Adventist message & mission to a global audience.
Students take stewardship of the Adventist message by publishing, presenting, or supporting content that customizes the medium for their intended audiences.
Students engage in a collaborative culture to create or support opportunities for ministry across all platforms.
Students exercise adaptive skills to refine products that effectively reach the intended community (global or local) through the appropriate technology mediums.

Students are aware of the privileges, responsibilities, and hazards of interacting in the digital environment, and are fluent in strategies for using netiquette - engaging in the digital environment safely and responsibly. (Digital Citizenship)
Students understand and accept the responsibility to use respectful language and images that edify others, not demean them (avoid cyberbullying).

Students practice safe data sharing, realizing that the digital footprint left behind is permanent, and can negatively affect their personal and reputational safety if information is not carefully guarded.
Students protect others' intellectual property by responsibly crediting sources and avoiding digital plagiarism.
Through collaboration, students engage with an authentic audience (globally or locally) by exploration, usage, and technological play with a variety of digital tools and media. (Global Collaborator)
Students use digital tools as a bridge to engage with learners from various backgrounds and/or cultures to broaden mutual understanding and learning.
Students use technologies to collaborate with peers, experts and/or community members, to examine issues and problems from a variety of viewpoints.
Students explore local and global issues and use collaborative technologies to work with others to investigate solutions.
Digital Learning
Students become adept at curating digital resources for a specific purpose, and at utilizing them to construct meaning and products that share that knowledge with others. (Knowledge Constructor)
Students learn how to use and manipulate key words to conduct internet searches and to intelligently filter results by judiciously evaluating the media's validity.
Students are proficient in how to electronically organize and store digital resources for future reference.
Students learn how to interpret text and other digital media and how to ethically incorporate that information into their own unique intellectual products.
Students establish and engage strategies for knowledge collection and determine ways that will guide the technology process to establish solutions. (Computational Thinker)
Students gather and classify information, using digital tools to investigate and present in a variety of ways to solve a problem or make a clear determination.
Students understand how automation works and use algorithmic thinking to develop a sequence of steps to create and test automated solutions such as robotics and coding.
Students create methods such as data analysis, hypothetical models, using algorithmic thinking in finding solutions.
Digital Fluency
Students will use various technologies within the design process to classify and then create new effective solutions for the growth and expansion of their digital learning. (Innovative Designer)
Students will use a calculated design process for producing testing theories and information, producing inventive resources, and real-world problems.
Students will use select media tools to execute the design process that recognizes the restrictions and uncertainties of design.
Students, as a part of the cyclical design process, develop, test, and refine prototypes, and work with open-ended problems.
Students design and construct products to communicate with authentic audiences clearly and creatively using a variety of media and digital tools appropriate to their goals. (Creative Communicator)
Students employ applicable platforms/tools to meet the intended objectives and audience of their creation or communication.
Students create and share original works or responsibly reshare digital resources into new creations for greater awareness.
Students communicate complex ideas clearly and effectively by through a variety of digital media.
